reading.title: A Map of the World
reading.text: Tom has a big map of the world on his bedroom wall. He puts a red pin in every country that he has read about. His uncle is a pilot, and he has flown all over the world. Last week the uncle brought Tom a small gift from Japan. Tom's dream is to travel round the world and see the biggest cities. He also enjoys watching the world news with his father, because it shows him how different life is in other countries.

listening.title: Planning a Trip
listening.script: Anna: I have just bought a book about the world's most famous places. Ben: Great! Where do you want to go first? Anna: I would like to see the pyramids in Egypt, because they are world-famous. After that I want to visit Australia. It is a very long way from here. Ben: You could travel round the world in six months if you save enough money. Anna: I am saving every month. My brother says it is the best way to see the world.

reading.title: Life in the Country
reading.text: Sara's family used to live in a big city, but last year they moved to the country. At first she missed her friends and the noisy streets. Now she loves country life. Every morning she walks along a country road to the school bus. Her father works on a farm in the south of the country, and her mother teaches in the village. At weekends the family travels across the country to visit Sara's grandmother, who lives in the capital.

listening.script: Teacher: Today Omar will tell us about his trip. Omar: Last summer I visited a foreign country for the first time. It was Turkey. I flew there with my uncle and we travelled across the country by bus. The roads were good, even the small country roads. I liked the people, but I missed my home country and my mother's food. Teacher: Would you go again? Omar: Yes, I want to see the north of the country next time.

reading.title: A New Start
reading.text: Leila left home last September to study in another city. At first she felt homesick and she called her parents every night. Her flat is small, but her roommate told her to make herself at home. Leila often cooks dishes from her home town because home cooking reminds her of her mother. Now she goes home once a month by bus. Her parents say that the house feels empty without her, but they are very proud.

listening.title: Working from Home
listening.script: Interviewer: Do you work in an office? Mr Karim: No, I work from home. I started last year. Interviewer: What do you like about it? Mr Karim: I can stay at home when the weather is bad, and I see my children when they come home from school. The only problem is that I sometimes feel lonely, so on Fridays I meet a friend in a cafe. Interviewer: Do you think you will go back to an office? Mr Karim: Not soon. I feel at home here.

reading.title: The Old Station
reading.text: In the centre of our town there is an old station. It is a historic building, and people say it was built in 1890. Last year the council wanted to tear it down and put up an office building. Many citizens did not agree, so they wrote letters and held a meeting. In the end the council decided to keep the station. Now builders are repairing the roof and the walls, and the building site is open to school visitors on Saturdays.

reading.title: Looking for a Flat
reading.text: Mina has just started working in a new city, so she needs to find accommodation. She looked at three flats to rent last weekend. The first one was too far from her office. The second was cheap, but the landlord wanted a deposit of two months' rent. The third flat was perfect: it is close to a metro station, and the monthly rent includes water and heating. Mina signed the contract on Monday, and she will move in next week.
